title: Uniform residue-field criterion for perfect ring complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $C\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $a\leq b$ be integers. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ put $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R/\mathfrak m$. Assume $H^i(C\otimes_R^L\kappa(\mathfrak m))=0$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$, where derived scalar extension is that of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $C$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and for every $R$-module $M$ one has $H^i(C\otimes_R^L M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P$ of $C$ using [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. A finite free module tensors as a finite direct sum, so tensoring preserves exact sequences coordinatewise. Thus [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P$ K-flat. Its conclusion is precisely ordinary-module K-flatness [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]: for every acyclic module complex $L$, the total tensor with $P$ is acyclic. On the identity-cover one-object site this is also the sheaf K-flat condition, since sections, tensor products and cohomology are the ordinary module operations. Thus [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] computes $C\otimes_R^L M$ by $P\otimes_R M[0]$ for every module $M$, including residue fields and localization rings. Fix also the following elementary fraction calculation for any module complex $T$ and multiplicative set $S$: $H^j(S^{-1}T)=S^{-1}H^j(T)$. Indeed a localized cycle $x/s$ has $t\,dx=0$ for some $t\in S$, so equals the localization of the cycle $tx$ divided by $ts$; if a cycle becomes a boundary, an equality $x/s=dy/u$ can be cleared by a further denominator, showing the class of $x/s$ is zero in localized cohomology. These give mutually inverse maps on cycles modulo boundaries. The same calculation applies to $T=P\otimes_R M$, and ordinary tensor associativity identifies its localization with $P_f\otimes_{R_f}M_f$. For scalar extension to a ring $S$, apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object ringed site with only identity covers: sheaves of modules are ordinary modules, and its K-flat calculation identifies $C\otimes_R^L S$ with $P\otimes_R S$ in $D(S)$, including the target module structure, not merely after restriction to $D(R)$.

proof.text: Fix $j\notin[a,b]$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Its residue-field vanishing, computed by step 1, permits [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-degree-cancellation] at degree $j$. For some $f\notin\mathfrak m$, $P_f$ is homotopy equivalent to a complex with zero term in degree $j$, so $H^j(P_f)=0$. Further localization at $\mathfrak m$ and the fraction calculation give $H^j(P)_{\mathfrak m}=0$. This holds for every maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to the zero map $H^j(P)\to0$: all its maximal localizations are bijective, hence it is bijective and $H^j(C)=H^j(P)=0$. This proves ordinary cohomology vanishing outside the interval, without assuming $C$ was bounded below.

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-degree-cancellation] to $P$ at $i=a-1$. It applies because $a-1<a$. Obtain $f\notin\mathfrak m$ and a bounded-above finite-free complex $Q$ with $Q^{a-1}=0$, homotopy equivalent to $P_f$. The zero middle term splits $Q$ as the direct sum of its terms in degrees $\leq a-2$ and in degrees $\geq a$; there are no cross differentials. The lower summand is acyclic: in each degree below $a-1$ its cohomology is that of $P_f$, which is zero by step 2 and the fraction calculation. Projection onto the upper summand $U$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $U$ represents $C_f$, is bounded and finite free, and is zero below $a$. No assertion that an acyclic complex stays acyclic under arbitrary ordinary tensor is used.

proof.text: Choose such $h_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal. The ideal generated by them is the unit ideal: otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] would put it in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, contradicting $h_{\mathfrak n}\notin\mathfrak n$. Membership of $1$ in the generated ideal is a finite linear combination, so finitely many $h_1,\ldots,h_r$ suffice. Every $C_{h_j}$ is perfect by its bounded finite-free representative in step 4 and [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] (finite free modules are finitely generated projective: lift the finitely many basis vectors through any surjection). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-ring-principal-cover-glue] to conclude $C$ is perfect. If $R$ is the zero ring, every unital $R$-module is zero and the conclusion holds directly, with an empty cover.

proof.text: Now let $M$ be any $R$-module and $j\notin[a,b]$. At a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ choose $h\notin\mathfrak m$ and $W$ as in step 4. The fraction calculation of step 1 and tensor associativity identify $H^j(P\otimes_R M)_h$ with $H^j(P_h\otimes_{R_h}M_h)$. Both $P_h$ and $W$ are bounded-above finite free, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]; by [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], their derived isomorphism as representatives of $C_h$ identifies this group with $H^j(W\otimes_{R_h}M_h)$. The latter is zero because its term in degree $j$ is zero. Further localization therefore gives $H^j(C\otimes_R^L M)_{\mathfrak m}=0$ for every maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to its zero map to conclude the group itself is zero. This proves the full uniform Tor conclusion.
